In 2008-style contagion events, even strong banks see multiple compression before fundamentals reassert.

verdict.headline: JPMorgan: relative safe haven in the SVB crisis, but NIM compression and contagion create real headwinds
verdict.summary: JPMorgan enters the SVB crisis from a position of balance-sheet strength [C8] — equity/assets at 8.4% and operating margin at 32.1% confirm it is not SVB. However, the collapse of SVB has triggered a 40bp fall in 10-year yields [C2], directly compressing JPM's net interest margin, and regional bank contagion [C6] (KRE down 24.8%) is dragging the entire financial sector lower. The evidence is mixed: JPM is outperforming XLF by 2.1pp [C5], suggesting flight-to-quality deposit inflows, but the broader sector sell-off and elevated VIX [C4] cap any near-term recovery. The scenario distribution is genuinely uncertain, with Mixed the plurality outcome.

key_drivers.point: 10y yields fell 40bp — NIM compression is the primary fundamental risk for JPM over 20 days.
KRE down 24.8%; contagion correlation 0.71 — sector-wide stress creates multiple compression even for strong banks.
VIX at 26.1 (74th percentile) — broad risk-off amplifies every other headwind.

counter_evidence.point: Equity/assets at 8.4% — fortress balance sheet; deposit inflows from fleeing SVB customers are a real tailwind.
Revenue +18.4% YoY and positive earnings surprise give JPM credibility as a safe harbor.

scenarios.name: Mixed
scenarios.rationale: Most likely: JPM outperforms sector but trades lower with it.

scenarios.name: Headwind-dominant
scenarios.rationale: Systemic contagion deepens; JPM multiple compressed despite fundamentals.
scenarios.watch_for: More bank failures; Fed emergency action.

scenarios.name: Tailwind-dominant
scenarios.rationale: Quick policy backstop and deposit inflow surge make JPM an outright winner.
scenarios.watch_for: FDIC / Fed announcement; deposit flow data.
